done_when: Every generated skill copy (.claude, .codex and .agents) comes from the same template text and describes the round rule the code applies; a test compares the copies; new repos get it at init and existing repos on upgrade and forge sync

known.title: Preserve existing .agents guides before replacing them
Gate: Existing sync and review-round guide tests fail

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Data loss
Case: normal use - An existing Forge client has team-maintained Forge pages under `.agents/skills/forge` and runs sync, upgrade, or migration.
This adds that previously unmanaged directory to the shipped files. `sync.write` overwrites differing content without preserving it (`src/forge/sync.py:595-602`), including ignored or uncommitted files during a direct sync. Migration also misses these pages: its preservation inventory covers the older `.claude` and `.codex` paths, but excludes `.agents` (`src/forge/migrate.py:85-90,229-249,652-653`). Team-specific instructions disappear from the active repo; untracked copies cannot be recovered from Git. The ruling to ship the companion pages did not address this collision.
Adds work: preserve previously unmanaged .agents pages before replacement; F 1 x H 1 = 1; 2 x C = 4
findings.title: Preserve existing .agents guides before replacing them

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Gate
Case: normal use - The pull request runs its related tests.
`tests/test_split_ships.py:19-24,71` expects an exact sync inventory containing only the `.claude` and `.codex` Forge pages, so the five new `.agents` pages make both cases fail. Separately, `tests/test_owner_decides_at_the_round_limit.py:254-264` still requires the sentence removed at this line, so both of its guide cases fail too. Both files import the changed `test_setup` module and are selected by the related-test picker, preventing the tests check from passing.
findings.title: Gate: Existing sync and review-round guide tests fail

why: The generated copies of the Forge skill in client repos disagree on the review round rule (one copy asks the owner after the second blocked round even for new findings, another describes P0 continuation)
